claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Optimizing the lamellar-colony architecture can reduce the number of internal boundaries.
Reducing internal boundaries will decrease microcrack initiation.
Reducing internal boundaries will decrease catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimizing the lamellar-colony architecture will improve strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Optimizing the lamellar-colony architecture will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Strength will improve by 15% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Room-temperature tensile ductility will improve by 15% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the optimized sample shows less than 10% improvement in both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 15% improvement in both properties, but falsification requires less than 10% improvement. Results from 10% to below 15% would fail the stated quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
